summary_zh: 本文概述了为2026年仁川RoboCup@Home公开平台联赛所开发的集成技术。集成基于学习且免训练模型的视觉系统，能够对已知与未知物体实现稳健识别。我们引入了一种基于RoomPlan的方法，半自动登记家具几何形状与标签，以生成语义地图。此外，基于大语言模型的规划器可解读由Whisper识别的指令，并生成供执行的基本技能序列。一种水库计算框架作为轻量级时间处理模型，用于动作识别。其基于现场可编程门阵列的实现，支持低功耗、实时运行。这对于消除服务机器人的运行时间限制至关重要。开源发布内容，包括任务环境、数据集工具及导航框架，增强了RoboCup@Home社区的可复现性、可复用性及持续进步。

title: Robot Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance from Randomly Positioned External Cameras
summary: We study robot navigation in indoor environments from fixed exocentric cameras (infrastructure-mounted, external to the robot). We show that standard Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which succeeds with onboard cameras, fails to learn this navigation end-to-end in our setup. This failure results from the perspective mismatch between exocentric observations and egocentric action and goal formulations, which is too complex to resolve from the reward signal alone. To address this, we propose Viewpoint-Invariant Navigation from Exocentric Cameras (VINE). VINE uses an obstacle map estimation network, trained with supervised learning, that takes exocentric images, camera pose, robot pose, and room dimensions as input and produces a viewpoint-invariant obstacle map. This map can be used either by a PPO policy or by a planner such as A*. VINE's map estimation performs better than perspective mapping approaches, handles cameras placed across a wide range of positions and orientations without view-specific tuning, requires only approximate camera pose estimates (noise with a standard deviation of 30cm per axis in x, y, and z and about 20° of rotation error on average), is robust to intrinsic variation, and extends to two-camera setups with partial coverage. Despite operating from cameras randomized in position during evaluation, VINE surpasses the navigation success rate of PPO with an onboard camera in simulated environments.
tldr: This paper introduces VINE, a method for robot navigation using external exocentric cameras that converts images to a viewpoint-invariant obstacle map via supervised learning, enabling PPO or A* planning and outperforming onboard-camera PPO despite randomized camera poses.
tldr_zh: 本文提出VINE方法，利用外部顶置摄像头通过监督学习生成视角不变的障碍物地图，使PPO或A*规划器能在随机相机位姿下完成导航，成功率超过车载相机PPO。
summary_zh: 我们研究了在固定外置摄像头（安装于基础设施上、机器人外部）环境下，机器人如何在室内环境中进行导航。我们发现，在机载摄像头下表现良好的标准近端策略优化（PPO）算法，在我们的设置中无法端到端地学习这一导航任务。这一失败源于外置视角观测与自我中心动作及目标表述之间的视角不匹配，这种不匹配过于复杂，无法仅通过奖励信号来解决。为此，我们提出了基于外置摄像头的视角不变导航方法（VINE）。VINE使用一个通过监督学习训练得到的障碍物地图估计网络，该网络输入外置图像、摄像头位姿、机器人位姿及房间尺寸，并生成一个视角不变的障碍物地图。该地图既可用于PPO策略，也可用于如A*等规划器。VINE的地图估计性能优于透视映射方法，能够适应各种位置和朝向的摄像头而无需针对特定视角进行调整，仅需近似摄像头位姿估计（x、y、z各轴噪声标准差为30厘米，平均旋转误差约20°），对内部参数变化具有鲁棒性，并可扩展到部分覆盖的双摄像头设置。尽管在评估时摄像头位置是随机化的，VINE在模拟环境中的导航成功率仍超过了使用机载摄像头的PPO方法。

title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence
summary: Generating diverse robot videos requires control over scene geometry, robot motion, and viewpoints. End-to-end video generation offers limited direct access to these variables, making targeted edits and reuse across tasks difficult. We present BWM-Forge, a code-driven framework for controllable video generation in robotics. Given robot assets and a task description, the framework accepts an initial image, an image with motion data, or a human demonstration video. A coding agent constructs editable Blender scene programs that specify objects, robot motion, and cameras. The resulting proxy videos provide structural and motion references for a video generation model, which adds visual detail. A multi-agent harness coordinates input processing, scene construction, review, and rendering. Automated evaluation and user feedback support iterative refinement, while an experience repository stores and retrieves reusable modeling and rendering rules. This design supports multiple robot embodiments, synchronized viewpoints, and appearance variation from a shared scene program. We evaluate the framework on 15 tasks covering five robot types. Compared with LingBot-World Base Cam on these tasks, BWM-Forge achieves higher aesthetic quality, imaging quality, subject and background consistency, motion smoothness, and RoboJudge-9B physical adherence and instruction alignment scores. The baseline scores higher in dynamic degree. Qualitative cases illustrate viewpoint control, scene variation, feedback-driven edits, and experience reuse across scenes. These results demonstrate a practical approach to generating controllable robot videos through editable, executable scene representations.
tldr: BWM-Forge is a code-driven framework that uses an agentic coding harness to generate editable Blender scene programs, which serve as structural and motion references for controllable robot video generation across multiple embodiments and tasks.
tldr_zh: BWM-Forge 是一个代码驱动框架，通过智能体编程生成可编辑的Blender场景程序，为多种机器人形态和任务的可控视频生成提供结构与运动参考。
summary_zh: 生成多样化的机器人视频需要对场景几何、机器人运动及视角进行精细控制。端到端的视频生成方法对这些变量的直接操控能力有限，难以实现跨任务的定向编辑与复用。我们提出BWM-Forge，一种面向机器人领域可控视频生成的代码驱动框架。该框架接受机器人资产和任务描述，可输入初始图像、带运动数据的图像或人类演示视频。框架中的编码智能体构建可编辑的Blender场景程序，用以指定物体、机器人运动及相机设置。生成的代理视频为视频生成模型提供结构与运动参考，模型进一步补充视觉细节。多智能体协作机制统筹输入处理、场景构建、审查与渲染流程。自动化评估与用户反馈支持迭代优化，经验库则存储并检索可复用的建模与渲染规则。该设计支持多种机器人形态、同步视角切换及基于共享场景程序的外观变化。我们在涵盖五种机器人类型的15项任务上对框架进行了评估。与LingBot-World Base Cam相比，BWM-Forge在美学质量、成像质量、主体与背景一致性、运动平滑度以及RoboJudge-9B物理遵从性和指令对齐得分上均表现更优；基线在动态程度上得分更高。定性案例展示了视角控制、场景变化、反馈驱动的编辑及跨场景经验复用效果。这些结果证明了通过可编辑、可执行的场景表示生成可控机器人视频的实用路径。

title: QVS-LIVO RiskMap: Health- and Information-Aware View Selection for Multi-Camera LIVO and Off-Road Risk Mapping
summary: Multi-camera observations in off-road environments vary significantly in reliability, posing challenges when complementing degraded geometric constraints. Motivated by this, we propose Quality-aware View Selection Lidar-Vision Odometry Risk Mapping (QVS-LIVO RiskMap), which decouples visual processing for state estimation from that for semantic mapping. The front end evaluates camera observations through read-only pretracking on a shared lidar-inertial posterior, combining observation health with geometric complementarity. Channel health memory and switching hysteresis govern selection of at most one eligible view for direct photometric correction. The posterior is retained when no view is eligible or the correction fails acceptance. The mapping back end integrates semantic observations from all available views in a shared world grid. Vehicle-scale geometry constrains semantic risk corrections, while spatial and temporal evidence supports risk confirmation. The system also produces a local bird's-eye-view (BEV) risk map and a global 2.5D semantic-terrain risk map with obstacle instance voxels. On two field sequences, QVS-LIVO achieved horizontal root mean square errors of 0.910 m and 1.664 m. It reduced error by 43.3% relative to FAST-LIO2 on the degraded long-route sequence. Across 12 controlled camera-fault configurations involving dropout, black frames and 60 ms timestamp shifts, it maintained complete trajectories with errors of 1.54-2.23 m. When deployed onboard an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the system generates local and global maps at 9.94 Hz and 2.00 Hz, respectively, with a median local mapping latency of 32.4 ms. These runtime results demonstrate the real-time feasibility of selective visual state updates alongside multi-view semantic mapping under challenging off-road conditions. The code and related resources are available at: https://github.com/zihanPan-HIT/QVS-LIVO.
tldr: This paper introduces QVS-LIVO RiskMap, a multi-camera LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry system with quality-aware view selection and risk mapping, demonstrating robust real-time performance on off-road field sequences with camera faults.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了 QVS-LIVO RiskMap，一种具有质量感知视角选择与风险地图构建的多相机 LiDAR-惯性-视觉里程计系统，在越野序列和相机故障下展示了鲁棒的实时性能。
summary_zh: 越野环境中的多相机观测可靠性差异显著，这为补充退化几何约束带来了挑战。为此，我们提出了一种质量感知视图选择的激光雷达-惯性-视觉里程计与风险地图构建方法（QVS-LIVO RiskMap），该方法将用于状态估计的视觉处理与用于语义建图的视觉处理解耦。前端通过共享的激光雷达-惯性后验状态进行只读预跟踪来评估相机观测，并结合观测健康度与几何互补性进行判断。通道健康记忆与切换迟滞机制控制着最多选择一个合格视图进行直接光度校正。当没有视图合格或校正未通过验收时，后验状态得以保留。建图后端在共享的世界栅格中融合来自所有可用视图的语义观测。车辆尺度几何约束用于限制语义风险校正，而空间与时间证据则支持风险确认。该系统同时生成局部鸟瞰图（BEV）风险地图和带有障碍物实例体素的全局2.5D语义-地形风险地图。在两个野外序列上，QVS-LIVO实现了0.910米和1.664米的水平均方根误差。在退化的长距离序列上，相比FAST-LIO2，误差降低了43.3%。在涉及丢失、黑帧和60毫秒时间戳偏移的12种受控相机故障配置下，系统保持了完整轨迹，误差范围为1.54至2.23米。当部署于NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin平台时，系统分别以9.94 Hz和2.00 Hz的频率生成局部和全局地图，局部建图延迟中位数为32.4毫秒。这些运行时结果证明了在具有挑战性的越野条件下，选择性视觉状态更新与多视角语义建图相结合的实时可行性。代码及相关资源可在以下网址获取：https://github.com/zihanPan-HIT/QVS-LIVO。

title: Runtime Safety and Emergency Stops on a Full-Size Humanoid: Deployment Lessons and a Case for Graduated Force Authority
summary: Full-size humanoid robots are being considered for hazardous industrial work such as disassembling electric-vehicle batteries. We describe the safety mechanisms of an open-source autonomy stack for the Unitree H1-2 humanoid and what deploying them taught us. All joint commands pass through a safety layer that runs separately from the control software. It enforces joint position, velocity, and torque limits, and it stops the robot when a state estimate becomes stale or when the hard-wired emergency stop (e-stop) is pressed or disconnected. We pushed the standing robot until it lost balance. With a model-predictive lower-body controller it never recovered, and the operator had to press the e-stop in every trial. Pressing it removes balance control, and the robot falls. The safety layer's own limits trigger the same stop, and limits chosen for manipulation were exceeded during normal walking. Near an operator or a battery pack, the fall can be more dangerous than the cause of the stop. Joint limits bound how much force a robot can apply, but not when applying it is appropriate. Drawing on research on responsibility and on child and adolescent development, we therefore make a case for granting robots force authority in stages, with a person or organization explicitly responsible for its use.
tldr: The paper discusses runtime safety mechanisms for a full-size humanoid robot, detailing lessons from deploying an autonomy stack and proposing a graduated force authority framework for safe operation.
tldr_zh: 该论文讨论了全尺寸人形机器人的运行时安全机制，详述了部署自主栈的经验，并提出了分级力量授权框架以确保安全操作。
summary_zh: 全尺寸人形机器人正被考虑用于危险工业工作，例如拆卸电动汽车电池。我们描述了面向Unitree H1-2人形机器人的开源自主栈的安全机制，以及部署这些机制所获得的经验。所有关节指令均经过一个独立于控制软件运行的安全层。该安全层强制执行关节位置、速度和力矩限制，并在状态估计过期或硬接线紧急停止（e-stop）按钮被按下或断开时使机器人停止运行。我们不断推挤站立中的机器人直至其失去平衡。在使用模型预测下半身控制器的情况下，机器人始终未能恢复平衡，操作员在每次试验中都必须按下紧急停止按钮。按下该按钮会解除平衡控制，机器人随即倒下。安全层自身的限制也会触发同样的停止，而在正常行走过程中，为操作任务设定的限制会被超出。在操作员或电池组附近，机器人倒下可能比触发停止的原因更具危险性。关节限制约束了机器人能够施加的力的大小，但并未规定何时施加这些力是恰当的。因此，借鉴关于责任感以及儿童和青少年发展的研究，我们主张分阶段授予机器人力的权限，并由个人或组织明确对其使用负责。

title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
summary: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io
tldr: This paper introduces DashBench, a benchmark for evaluating Video LLMs' understanding of corner cases in autonomous driving, finding that current models perform inadequately for safety-critical applications.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了DashBench，一个用于评估视频大语言模型在自动驾驶中边缘案例理解能力的基准，发现当前模型在安全关键应用中表现不足。
summary_zh: 现代视频大语言模型（Video LLMs）所承诺的自然语言解释，为自动驾驶系统提供了一条通往详细场景描述和道路上可解释决策的路径。尽管近期已有基准测试开始评估这些模型在驾驶场景中的表现，但这些测试主要基于现有驾驶数据集，针对常规交通状况和一般理解任务，因此未能评估模型在最罕见且最关键的安全驾驶事件（即“边缘案例”）上的表现。为了在这些特定场景下对视频大语言模型进行全面评估，我们引入了DashBench，这是一个基准测试，涵盖25个视频大语言模型，涉及1，709个精心挑选的驾驶视频，不仅包括与碰撞相关的边缘案例，还包括罕见的非碰撞案例。通过大量提示和开放式问答，我们揭示了一个关键的能力差距：所有被评估的模型表现都远低于安全关键驾驶应用所需的阈值，频繁误判或遗漏前方道路上的危险事件，并在其解释中幻觉出不存在的代理或动作。我们相信，DashBench结合了广泛的数据集、严格的评估工具包以及对当前模型局限性的详细诊断，将推动朝着更安全、更可解释的自动驾驶系统迈进。代码和数据将在以下地址共享：cornercase-dashbench.github.io

title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
summary: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. We introduce HeMeR, an inference framework that performs KV reconciliation between dynamically updated memory contexts and reusable KV states. HeMeR tracks declarative, procedural, and working memory contents across action decisions, preserves KV states for unchanged contents, and reconciles only the KV states affected by memory-content updates. This enables efficient and stable inference as memory contents evolve during interaction. We evaluate HeMeR on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robotic deployments requiring coordinated use of heterogeneous memory contents. In the real-world setting, HeMeR achieves 83.20% task success and reduces per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL, while preserving compatible KV states as task progress updates the memory context.
tldr: HeMeR is an inference framework enabling efficient KV cache reuse across heterogeneous memory modules for embodied agents. It reduces per-step inference time while preserving performance on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real robots.
tldr_zh: HeMeR 是一个推理框架，通过异构记忆模块间的 KV 缓存复用，在保持性能的同时降低具身智能体的推理时间。
summary_zh: 具身智能体通过整合来自异构记忆模块的信息来进行决策，包括用于显性知识的陈述性记忆、用于习得性程序性记忆以及用于当前观察的工作记忆。在交互过程中，决策所需的记忆内容会随着智能体的状态、目标和任务进展而变化，但许多内容在连续决策中仍然保持共享。然而，现有记忆模块通常通过独立的接口访问，因此每次更新的记忆上下文往往被作为基础模型的新输入处理。这阻碍了对未变化记忆内容进行选择性键值（KV）缓存复用，并导致即使在大量记忆上下文仍然有效的情况下，也必须进行完整的KV缓存重计算。我们提出了HeMeR，一个推理框架，它在动态更新的记忆上下文与可复用KV状态之间进行KV调和。HeMeR在动作决策过程中跟踪陈述性记忆、程序性记忆和工作记忆的内容，保留未变化内容的KV状态，并仅调和受记忆内容更新影响的KV状态。这使得在交互过程中记忆内容演变时，推理既能高效又能保持稳定。我们在ALFWorld、Habitat以及需要协调使用异构记忆内容的真实机器人部署中对HeMeR进行了评估。在真实场景中，与MemRL相比，HeMeR实现了83.20%的任务成功率，并将每步推理时间从2.94秒降低至1.87秒，同时在任务进展更新记忆上下文时保持了兼容的KV状态。

title: Fog-FWL: A Large-Scale Full-Waveform LiDAR Dataset for Recovering Fog-Hidden Objects
summary: LiDAR is a core sensor for autonomous driving, yet it is highly vulnerable to fog. Fog scattering produces strong backscatter near the sensor and attenuates reflections from objects behind it, so weak object returns are often discarded by the peak detection that converts received signals into point clouds. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL), which records the received optical signal before peak detection, retains these weak returns, but the lack of suitable data has prevented research on recovering fog-hidden objects from FWL. We present Fog-FWL, a dataset foundation for this task that consists of a real-world benchmark, Fog-FWL-Real, and a large-scale synthetic training set, Fog-FWL-Sim. Fog-FWL-Real contains 7,527 real foggy FWL frames from 8 scenes and 58 sequences, which is 579x larger than the only existing real foggy FWL data, together with histogram-level Object/Fog/Noise labels, 10,719 3D bounding boxes, and three difficulty levels defined by the attenuation of object reflections. Fog-FWL-Sim contains 12,000 frames generated by our physics-based simulator, Fog-FWL-Simulator, which integrates spatially heterogeneous fog density fields, time-resolved light transport including multiple scattering, and a photon-counting SPAD receiver model. The two subsets share the same sensor format and annotation protocol, enabling a strict sim-to-real evaluation in which no real waveforms are used for training. Our analysis shows that, under the hardest condition, object returns are included in the three strongest peaks for only 34.9% of object rays, underscoring the need for waveform-level recovery. Fog-FWL-Real, Fog-FWL-Sim, and the Fog-FWL-Simulator will be publicly released to facilitate research on fog-robust LiDAR perception.
tldr: Fog-FWL introduces the first large-scale real and synthetic full-waveform LiDAR dataset, paired with a physics-based simulator, to enable recovery of fog-hidden objects for autonomous driving perception.
tldr_zh: Fog-FWL 提出了首个大规模真实与合成全波形 LiDAR 数据集，并配套物理仿真器，用于恢复自动驾驶感知中被雾隐藏的物体。
summary_zh: 激光雷达是自动驾驶的核心传感器，然而其极易受雾天影响。雾的散射会在传感器附近产生强后向散射，同时衰减其后物体的反射信号，因此较弱的物体回波在将接收信号转换为点云的峰值检测过程中常被丢弃。全波形激光雷达（FWL）在峰值检测之前记录接收到的光信号，能够保留这些弱回波，但由于缺乏合适的数据，从全波形数据中恢复被雾遮挡物体的研究一直无从开展。我们提出Fog-FWL，为该任务提供数据集基础，包含一个真实世界基准数据集Fog-FWL-Real和一个大规模合成训练集Fog-FWL-Sim。Fog-FWL-Real包含来自8个场景、58个序列的7，527帧真实雾天全波形数据，其规模是现有唯一真实雾天全波形数据的579倍，同时提供直方图级别的物体/雾/噪声标签、10，719个三维边界框，以及根据物体反射衰减程度划分的三个难度级别。Fog-FWL-Sim包含由我们的物理仿真器Fog-FWL-Simulator生成的12，000帧数据，该仿真器集成了空间异构雾密度场、包含多次散射的时间分辨光传输模型，以及光子计数SPAD接收器模型。两个子集共享相同的传感器格式和标注协议，可实现严格的仿真到真实迁移评估，其中不使用任何真实波形进行训练。我们的分析表明，在最困难的条件下，仅34.9%的物体射线其回波包含在三个最强峰值中，这凸显了波形级恢复的必要性。Fog-FWL-Real、Fog-FWL-Sim及Fog-FWL-Simulator将公开发布，以促进抗雾鲁棒激光雷达感知的研究。

title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
summary: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.
tldr: This paper introduces a data-efficient training and control architecture for imitating nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) using neural networks, validated on a real Furuta pendulum, achieving a 1 kHz control frequency and matching the expert's region of attraction.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种数据高效的训练与控制架构，用于用神经网络模仿非线性时间最优模型预测控制（TOMPC），并在真实的Furuta摆上验证，实现了1 kHz的控制频率并匹配专家的吸引域。
summary_zh: 非线性时间最优模型预测控制（TOMPC）能够在约束系统上实现高性能控制，但其计算成本使得在快速动态系统上的实时应用受到限制。通过神经网络对TOMPC控制律进行模仿可降低在线计算成本，然而现有工作大多针对仿真中的二次代价形式，并且孤立地处理神经控制器面临的挑战。本文对带有硬终端约束的长时域非凸TOMPC进行模仿，其高计算成本限制了训练数据的生成。我们提出：(i) 自信息采样（SIFS）——一种数据高效的专家采样策略，利用学习得到的剩余时间量，仅在策略偏离时间最优行为时才对专家进行查询；(ii) 一套完整的训练与控制架构，联合处理数据集相关性、次优专家标签、协变量偏移、约束满足和模型失配问题；以及(iii) 在Furuta摆上的实际系统验证。SIFS在训练时间约为原有方法三分之一、训练数据少于一半的情况下达到了与标准数据集聚合相当的性能。所得控制器能够匹配专家TOMPC的吸引域，同时将控制频率从1.4Hz提升至1kHz。在硬件实验中，该控制器能够沿与专家TOMPC解高度一致的轨迹完成摆的摆起与稳定控制。

title: AgriSense: Vision-Language Decision Support and Robotic Intervention in a Virtual Greenhouse Copy title
summary: Autonomous greenhouse management increasingly requires robotic systems that integrate perception, navigation, environmental regulation, and plant-level intervention. This paper presents AgriSense, a framework combining an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, RGB and LiDAR-inertial sensing, environmental control, and supervised vision-language decision support. Frozen DINOv2 and BERT encoders, together with structured environmental inputs, support joint prediction of twelve environmental references, a target zone, and an intervention flag. Checkpoint replay reproduces 41/43 zone decisions. Across five seeds on a source-grouped test set, the full, image-removed, and language-removed configurations each achieve 43/44 correct zone decisions, providing no evidence of incremental multimodal zone-accuracy improvement. The full model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.249 degrees C for temperature, 2.030 percentage points for humidity, and 0.997 percentage points for soil moisture. Sensor-only inputs match full-model zone accuracy, while language-only inputs achieve 68.64%. External real-image benchmarks reveal distribution-shift limitations. Five offline Point-LIO routes yield rigidly aligned trajectory errors of 5.22-17.32 mm. Of 40 virtual-arm targets, 32 satisfy geometric acceptance criteria and eight are rejected at boundaries. Six long-horizon climate cases and fault protocols characterize integration limits. Navigation and integrated treatment rely on simulator-state inputs; physical greenhouse performance and agronomic treatment efficacy remain unvalidated. The contribution is an evaluated decision-support and robotic-intervention framework for a virtual greenhouse.
tldr: AgriSense presents a simulated greenhouse with a quadruped robot, integrating vision-language decision support and robotic intervention, but shows limited multimodal gains and lacks real-world validation.
tldr_zh: AgriSense 提出了一个模拟温室环境，集成四足机器人、视觉语言决策支持与机器人干预，但多模态增益有限且缺乏真实世界验证。
summary_zh: 自主温室管理日益需要整合感知、导航、环境调控及植株级干预的机器人系统。本文提出了AgriSense框架，该框架结合了Isaac Sim虚拟温室、四足移动操作平台、RGB与激光雷达-惯性传感、环境控制以及监督式视觉-语言决策支持。冻结的DINOv2和BERT编码器结合结构化环境输入，支持对十二项环境参考指标、目标区域及干预标志的联合预测。检查点回放正确复现了41/43的区域决策。在基于源分组的测试集上跨越五种随机种子，完整配置、去除图像配置及去除语言配置均实现了43/44的正确区域决策，未发现多模态融合对区域精度有增量提升的证据。完整模型在温度、湿度和土壤湿度上的平均绝对误差分别为0.249摄氏度、2.030个百分点和0.997个百分点。仅传感器输入达到了与完整模型相同的区域精度，而仅语言输入仅达到68.64%的精度。外部真实图像基准测试揭示了分布偏移的局限性。五条离线Point-LIO路径的刚体对齐轨迹误差为5.22至17.32毫米。在40个虚拟机械臂目标中，32个满足几何接受标准，8个在边界处被拒绝。六个长时域气候案例和故障协议刻画了系统集成的局限性。导航和综合处理依赖于模拟器状态输入；物理温室性能和农艺处理效果尚未得到验证。本文的贡献在于为虚拟温室提供了一个经过评估的决策支持与机器人干预框架。

title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents
summary: Long-term spacecraft autonomy requires embodied agents to use operational history under communication delays, time-critical operations, environmental uncertainty, complex physical interactions, power and computational constraints, and safety and reliability requirements. We introduce AstroMemBench and a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method that maps these requirements to executable memory tests. The benchmark covers 16 memory subchallenges through 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration. A deterministic environment scores actions for task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations under nine conditions show that the benchmark is sensitive to how accurately agents recover and use historical information and to differences in memory-system design. Main experiments compare six configurations. Mem0, Chain-of-Memory, LightMem, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improve same-session mean scores over native Pi Agent, with no clear advantage of the three memory systems over RAG. After a session restart, Mem0 outperforms RAG by 12.25 points. Benefits favor instruction retention and result reuse over ongoing state tracking and energy reservation. AstroMemBench supports the design, development, and selection of memory systems for embodied spacecraft agents. AstroMemBench 1.0 and its evaluation code are publicly available: https://github.com/flyingView/AstroMemBench-v1.
tldr: AstroMemBench introduces a benchmark for evaluating memory systems in embodied spacecraft agents, covering 16 subchallenges via 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks, with a deterministic scoring environment and experiments showing sensitivity to memory designs and benefits for instruction retention and result reuse.
tldr_zh: AstroMemBench 提出了一个用于评估具身航天器代理中记忆系统的基准，通过九个任务中的140个模板和2240个实例覆盖16个记忆子挑战，并提供确定性评分环境，实验表明其对记忆设计敏感且有利于指令保持和结果重用。
summary_zh: 长期航天器自主运行要求具身智能体在通信延迟、时间关键操作、环境不确定性、复杂物理交互、功耗与计算约束以及安全可靠性要求下，利用运行历史进行决策。我们提出AstroMemBench基准及其场景-挑战-能力设计方法，将上述需求映射为可执行的记忆测试。该基准涵盖行星表面操作、在轨服务与深空探测三大领域的九项任务，通过140个模板和2240个实例覆盖16项记忆子挑战。确定性环境根据任务完成度、状态变化、安全性和资源使用情况对动作进行评分。在九种条件下的消融实验表明，该基准对智能体准确恢复和利用历史信息的能力以及记忆系统设计差异具有敏感性。主要实验比较了六种配置。Mem0、Chain-of-Memory、LightMem和检索增强生成（RAG）在同期会话中的平均得分均优于原生Pi Agent，但三种记忆系统相比RAG并无明显优势。会话重启后，Mem0比RAG高出12.25分。其优势更侧重于指令保持和结果复用，而非持续状态跟踪和能量预留。AstroMemBench为具身航天器智能体记忆系统的设计、开发和选型提供支持。AstroMemBench 1.0及其评估代码已公开：https://github.com/flyingView/AstroMemBench-v1

title: COMBS: Concealed Object Multi-modal Bayesian Search
summary: This work addresses the problem of finding a concealed object in an environment by unifying formalisms for partially observable environments with multi-modal priors drawn from a mix of ontologies, semantic networks, LLMs, and VLMs. We propose a concealment-adaptive mixed-observability MDP (CA-MOMDP), a Bayes-adaptive setting where uncertainty is over both object locations and which nodes can conceal them, held as a hypothesis with a bounded ontology prior and resolved only by interaction. We define a hierarchical transition system (HTS) to abstract the environment into room and object nodes that can be planned over via our CA-MOMDP. We further propose a COMBS-score: a multi-modal fusion of a human informed semantic network, LLM, and VLM, to initialize the belief over object locations, which grounds our abstractions and reduces reliance on a single model. Belief is maintained via Bayes' rule, which never lets a look rule out a closed container. We prove a present target is found in a bounded number of searches under exact perception and that its location is never ruled out given missed detection under noisy perception. We ablate each component to demonstrate their significance. Across five simulator configurations, from a gridworld to Matterport3D with a real detector, COMBS finds 92-100% of in-distribution and 92-100% of out-of-distribution targets, matches or beats the baselines in processing speed, significantly outperforms a per-step LLM policy at lower cost on the larger scenes, recovers more out-of-distribution placements than a TidyBot ranking, and matches an LLM-only prior at a fraction of its per-decision latency. COMBS is the only standalone method that can declare a target absent at a stated error level, and the per-step LLM policy offered a termination action abandons 12-22% of targets that were present, against 1.6-3.2% for COMBS on the same episodes.
tldr: COMBS proposes a Bayes-adaptive MDP framework with multi-modal LLM/VLM priors for efficient and reliable concealed object search in 3D environments, demonstrating high success rates and bounded-time guarantees.
tldr_zh: COMBS 提出了一种基于贝叶斯自适应 MDP 与多模态 LLM/VLM 先验的隐藏物体搜索框架，在 3D 环境中实现了高成功率与有界时间保证。
summary_zh: 本研究旨在解决在部分可观测环境中定位隐蔽目标的问题，通过将部分可观测环境的 formalism 与来自本体论、语义网络、大语言模型（LLM）及视觉语言模型（VLM）的多模态先验信息相统一。我们提出了一种隐蔽自适应混合可观测马尔可夫决策过程（CA-MOMDP），这是一种贝叶斯自适应框架，其中不确定性同时涉及目标位置和哪些节点可以隐藏目标，这些信息以带有有界本体先验的假设形式存在，且仅能通过交互来消解。我们定义了一个层次化转移系统（HTS），将环境抽象为可经由CA-MOMDP进行规划的“房间”节点与“物体”节点。此外，我们提出了COMBS评分：一种融合人类知识语义网络、LLM和VLM的多模态打分机制，用于初始化目标位置的信念分布，从而为我们的抽象提供依据，并减少对单一模型的依赖。信念通过贝叶斯规则进行更新，该规则确保“查看”操作永远不会排除封闭容器内的目标。我们证明了在精确感知条件下，现存目标必然在有限次搜索内被发现；而在噪声感知条件下，即使检测发生漏报，目标位置也永远不会被排除。我们对各组件进行了消融实验，以展示其各自的重要性。在从网格世界到配备真实检测器的Matterport3D的五个模拟器配置中，COMBS对分布内目标实现了92-100%的发现率，对分布外目标亦实现了92-100%的发现率；其处理速度与基线方法持平或优于基线；在更大场景中，以更低的成本显著优于逐步LLM策略；恢复了比TidyBot排序更多的分布外目标放置位置；并且以仅LLM先验的一小部分决策延迟达到了与其相当的性能。COMBS是唯一能够以指定错误水平声明目标不存在的独立方法，而逐步LLM策略提供的终止动作在同一测试场景中会放弃12-22%实际存在的目标，相比之下，COMBS仅放弃1.6-3.2%。

title: Where to Generate Touch: Do Image Latents Preserve Material Recognition?
summary: Generated touch could extend robot learning beyond recorded contacts. A tactile generator needs a latent space, and we choose one by testing whether a material classifier trained on real GelSight presses still works on encode-decode reconstructions from pretrained image models. On ObjectFolder Real, the classifier loses 6.5 to 9.7 points on reconstructions from three 16x discrete tokenizers and 0.3 points on those from the Stable Diffusion VAE (SD-VAE). The 16x tokenizers again lose far more on Touch and Go and on DIGIT object recognition (YCB-Slide). Retraining the classifier on reconstructions, with no new labels, narrows the discrete gap. SD-VAE reconstructions also keep object identity, with 76.7% object-matching accuracy against 78.9% for real touch and 67.0% for MAGVIT-v2. We therefore select SD-VAE latents and show a photo-to-touch generator trained in them. Code will be released upon acceptance.
tldr: This paper evaluates latent spaces from pretrained image models for touch generation by testing material recognition on reconstructions, finding SD-VAE preserves touch and object identity best, and trains a photo-to-touch generator in SD-VAE latents.
tldr_zh: 本文通过测试重建触觉上的材料识别，评估预训练图像模型的潜在空间用于触觉生成，发现SD-VAE最保留触觉和物体身份，并在其潜在空间中训练照片到触觉生成器。
summary_zh: 生成的触觉可以将机器人学习扩展到记录的接触之外。触觉生成器需要潜在空间，我们通过测试基于真实GelSight按压训练的材料分类器是否仍能在预训练图像模型的编解码重建上工作来选择潜在空间。在ObjectFolder Real数据集上，分类器在三种16倍离散分词器的重建上损失6.5至9.7分，而在Stable Diffusion VAE（SD-VAE）的重建上仅损失0.3分。16倍分词器在Touch and Go和DIGIT物体识别（YCB-Slide）上损失更大。在重建上重新训练分类器，无需新标签，缩小了离散分词器的差距。SD-VAE重建还保持了物体身份，其物体匹配准确率为76.7%，而真实触觉为78.9%，MAGVIT-v2为67.0%。因此，我们选择SD-VAE潜在空间，并展示了一个在此空间中训练的从照片到触觉的生成器。代码将在论文被接收后发布。

title: Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
summary: Reconstructing dynamic scenes and objects from monocular egocentric video is crucial for embodied AI, yet existing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approaches struggle with everyday interactions involving topological changes, such as cutting, assembly, opening, or closing. Since 4DGS methods rely on deforming a fixed representation, events that split, merge, or reveal surfaces cause severe visual artifacts. To address this challenge, we introduce TopoEgo, the first benchmark dedicated to topological changes in egocentric video (covering fission, fusion, open, and close), alongside Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware reconstruction method. Topo4DGS jointly models part-level motion and time-varying surface support by assigning independent rigid transformations to interacting parts and dynamically activating or deactivating Gaussians as surfaces appear, disappear, or separate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Topo-4DGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 4DGS approaches across topological changes, especially on post-event frames. Code and data will be made publicly available.
tldr: Introduces TopoEgo, a benchmark for topological changes in egocentric video, and Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware 4D Gaussian Splatting method that models part-level motion and dynamically activates/deactivates Gaussians for improved reconstruction of dynamic scenes.
tldr_zh: 介绍了用于自我中心视频中拓扑变化基准的TopoEgo，以及Topo-4DGS，一种拓扑感知的4D高斯泼溅方法，通过建模部件级运动和动态激活/停用高斯来改进动态场景重建。
summary_zh: 从单目第一人称视频中重建动态场景和对象对于具身人工智能至关重要，然而现有的4D高斯泼溅（4DGS）方法在处理涉及拓扑变化的日常交互（如切割、组装、打开或关闭）时面临困难。由于4DGS方法依赖于对固定表示的变形，分裂、合并或暴露表面的事件会造成严重的视觉伪影。为应对这一挑战，我们引入了TopoEgo——首个专门针对第一人称视频中拓扑变化（涵盖分裂、融合、打开和关闭）的基准，以及Topo-4DGS——一种拓扑感知的重建方法。Topo-4DGS通过为交互部件分配独立的刚体变换，并在表面出现、消失或分离时动态激活或停用高斯体，联合建模部件级运动与时变表面支撑。大量实验表明，Topo-4DGS在拓扑变化场景中显著优于最先进的4DGS方法，尤其在事件后帧上的表现更为突出。代码和数据将公开发布。

title: Imitating the Imperfect: Offline-to-Online Robust Imitation Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrators
summary: Imitation learning (IL) typically relies on large-scale offline demonstrations collected from multiple human or algorithmic demonstrators. However, most existing approaches assume these demonstrators are homogeneous or near-optimal experts, a convenient but unrealistic assumption in real-world applications. In practice, demonstrations are often collected from heterogeneous demonstrators with unknown and varying levels of expertise, resulting in highly mixed-quality data. In this work, we study a challenging yet practical setting of imitation learning from such heterogeneous imperfect demonstrators. We propose Latent Expertise and Optimality Scoring based Imitation Learning (LEOS-IL), a principled framework that jointly learns (i) a state-action optimality scoring model and (ii) latent expertise levels for each demonstrator from unlabeled suboptimal offline demonstrations. The learned scoring model is then integrated into an online policy optimization procedure, where the agent is trained to maximize estimated optimality scores while its online rollouts are iteratively leveraged to refine the scoring model, thereby mitigating distributional shift during online adaptation. We further provide theoretical guarantees for optimality score identification and conditional optimal occupancy and policy recovery under explicit sufficient conditions. Experiments on continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines across highly heterogeneous and low-quality demonstration regimes.
tldr: LEOS-IL introduces a framework for imitation learning from heterogeneous, suboptimal demonstrations by jointly learning optimality scores and latent expertise levels to train robust policies in continuous control.
tldr_zh: LEOS-IL 提出了一种从异质、次优演示中学习模仿的框架，通过联合学习最优性评分和隐式专业水平来训练鲁棒策略，并在连续控制任务中验证。

title: CT-SGAL-LIO: Causal Continuous Time Refinement of Discrete LiDAR Inertial Odometry
summary: State-of-the-art LiDAR-inertial odometry methods, including those on richer state manifolds, achieve strong global accuracy, yet their pose stream alternates between propagation and correction and can oscillate over short horizons even when globally accurate. Most existing methods follow these approaches: they either modify the filter to enable faster updates or estimate a continuous-time trajectory from raw LiDAR and inertial data. The latter involves extra optimization, delaying state updates and becoming less robust during rapid rotations or accelerations. We propose CT-SGAL-LIO, a continuous-time refinement module that smooths the posterior pose stream of a discrete SGal(3) estimator without modifying the estimator itself. The key novelty is to perform continuous-time trajectory refinement directly on the projected SGal(3) posterior: we fit a cubic trajectory over a bounded window of recent poses and evaluate it at a small fixed lag. This places the query time within the observed interval, so the refined pose is obtained by interpolation rather than extrapolation, while preserving causal operation. CT-SGAL-LIO improves relative trajectory accuracy on 17 sequences from three public benchmarks. Across 17 sequences from GRAND-TOUR, MCD, and GEODE, CT-SGAL-LIO improves short-term motion accuracy while largely preserving global accuracy. RTE improves by up to 70% on GRAND-TOUR and on all seven GEODE sequences, with 9.9-51.1% reductions. A 19.5-min R-Campus run also reduces posterior jumps by 85.4% with only a 4.7 mm change in the end-to-start gap. We plan to release our source code and results to support community validation and reproducibility.
tldr: CT-SGAL-LIO introduces a continuous-time refinement module that smooths the pose stream from a discrete LiDAR-inertial estimator by fitting a cubic trajectory over recent poses in a causal, fixed-lag manner, improving relative trajectory accuracy while preserving global accuracy.
tldr_zh: CT-SGAL-LIO 提出一种连续时间细化模块，通过对近期位姿进行三次轨迹拟合并以固定滞后因果插值，平滑离散 LiDAR-惯性估计器的位姿流，在保持全局精度的同时提高相对轨迹精度。

title: A Class of Bayesian Conjugate Distributions on $SE_n(3)$ for Motion Estimation
summary: This paper proposes a novel class of Bayesian Conjugate Distributions (BCDs) on extended special Euclidean groups SE_n(3) for global motion uncertainty representation and estimation. BCDs are constructed by restricting matrix Gaussian distributions on ambient Euclidean space to SE_n(3), avoiding singularity of local coordinates. The unique feature of BCDs is their conjugacy to a broad class of sampling distributions arising in motion estimation, enabling exact closed-form Bayesian inference. Optimal estimation with respect to BCDs is further investigated for implementing motion estimation. Two means are extracted as random state estimates, which maximize probability and minimize mean squared error, respectively. Moreover, within the BCD class, moment matching is shown to minimize the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and maximum likelihood estimation is also derived, which provide analytical methods to approximate underlying distributions with the optimality guarantee. As an application, a Bayesian estimator for pose and velocity estimation of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is developed within an assumed density filtering architecture. The propagation and estimate extraction leverage the optimal estimation related to BCDs, and the landmark measurements are exactly fused with the BCD prior in closed form due to the conjugacy. Numerical simulations of a UAV flight indicate the advantages of BCD-based estimators over two classic Kalman filters on Lie groups with various initial uncertainties and measurement noise.
tldr: This paper introduces a new class of Bayesian Conjugate Distributions on SE_n(3) for global motion uncertainty representation and estimation, enabling closed-form Bayesian inference and applied to UAV pose and velocity estimation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一类在SE_n(3)上的贝叶斯共轭分布，用于全局运动不确定性表示与估计，实现闭式贝叶斯推断，并将其应用于无人机位姿和速度估计。

title: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field
summary: We introduce CABOT, a computational model for autonomous mobile robots in which the discrete plane the robots operate on is not a passive stage but an active computing medium. In the classical Look-Compute-Move (LCM) model every increase in computational capability is obtained by strengthening the robots themselves, with lights, memory or wider visibility, at a cost paid once per robot. CABOT strengthens the environment instead: each cell of the grid holds a state from a finite set Q, the states evolve synchronously under a uniform local rule that also senses whether a robot stands on the cell, that is, the floor is a cellular automaton, and the Look operation returns the states of the visible cells in addition to the positions of the visible robots. The robots are as weak as we can make them: oblivious, silent, lightless, myopic with visibility range 1, without multiplicity detection and unable to write to the floor. The number of field states |Q|, rather than any robot capability, becomes the measure of the resources required. On an inert floor (|Q| = 1) such robots can neither form a line, nor gather from scattered positions, nor explore a grid. We show that a handful of states changes this. Line Formation from connected configurations is solvable with four states, and field-silently, so that the floor also reaches a fixed point, with five. Gathering from arbitrary, possibly disconnected, configurations is solvable with three states and Line Formation from arbitrary configurations with six; we prove that neither can be solved field-silently with any number of states. A single robot explores every finite grid forever with four states and every torus with two, which is optimal. Further rule sets, validated by simulation only, equalize the spacing of robots on a row, fill a pattern painted on the floor and guide robots through a maze, and indicate the range of the model.
tldr: This paper introduces CABOT, a computational model for autonomous mobile robots where the environment (grid floor) acts as an active computing medium via cellular automaton states, enabling weak robots to solve tasks like line formation, gathering, and exploration with a few field states.
tldr_zh: 本文提出CABOT，一种自主移动机器人计算模型，其中环境（网格地面）通过元胞自动机状态作为主动计算介质，使弱机器人仅用少量状态即可完成列队、聚集和探索等任务。

title: RGB-D SLAM on the Edge: Benchmarking and Profiling RTAB-Map and ORB-SLAM3 on the Raspberry Pi 5
summary: Micro aerial vehicles that operate without GPS often run SLAM on ARM-based edge boards, yet there is little published data on how standard RGB-D SLAM systems behave on such hardware. We benchmark RTAB-Map and ORB-SLAM3 on the Raspberry Pi 5 using six TUM RGB-D sequences at three image resolutions, recording tracking coverage, trajectory error, time per frame, memory, CPU load and temperature for every run, and we profile both systems at the stage and function level. RTAB-Map was configured to process and keep every frame, so its back end runs on every frame rather than at its default rate of 1 Hz. On the sequences that every configuration tracked, its front end takes 38-74 ms per frame and its full pipeline 150-462 ms, compared with 13-45 ms and 26-62 ms for ORB-SLAM3. RTAB-Map's main cost is optimizing a pose graph that keeps growing, because its working memory is unbounded by default; ORB-SLAM3's local bundle adjustment costs about as much as its tracking but runs in a parallel thread. At quarter resolution, both systems lose tracking on most sequences, and runs that lose tracking finish sooner and report lower error on the poses they keep, so time and accuracy must be read alongside coverage. Timing is repeatable to within 1-5%, but trajectory error varies by up to 27% between identical runs, so the accuracy differences between the two systems are inconclusive. No thermal throttling occurred.
tldr: This paper benchmarks and profiles two standard RGB-D SLAM systems (RTAB-Map and ORB-SLAM3) on the Raspberry Pi 5 edge board, providing detailed performance data on tracking coverage, latency, memory, CPU, and temperature.
tldr_zh: 本文在树莓派5边缘计算板上对两种标准RGB-D SLAM系统（RTAB-Map和ORB-SLAM3）进行了基准测试和性能剖析，提供了跟踪覆盖率、延迟、内存、CPU和温度等详细性能数据。

title: A Coupled Control Barrier Function Approach to Deadlock-Free Multi-Robot Conflict Resolution
summary: Many robotic applications involve scenarios where multiple robots interact and the decisions of one robot influence the behavior of others. This paper presents a quadratic programming (QP)-based feedback controller for multi-robot conflict resolution with input constraints. Safety is enforced using coupled Control Barrier Function (CBF), while a yielding matrix encodes how robots influence each other. Unlike existing methods with fixed or hard priorities, the proposed framework enables yielding preferences while guaranteeing deadlock-free operation by design. Sufficient conditions are established for the controller to be locally Lipschitz. The optimal CBF sign- indefinite slack is shown to admit a finite uniform bound, which is compensated through an enlarged CBF safety margin to obtain a forward invariant set contained within the desired safe set. The analysis also identifies an irreducible slack component due to finite maximum deceleration that cannot be eliminated by increasing the slack penalty. Finally, sufficient conditions on the yielding matrix and nominal controller are derived to exclude deadlock states. Simulations demonstrate adaptive coordination across yielding preferences and robustness to robot failures.
tldr: This paper proposes a QP-based feedback controller using coupled Control Barrier Functions and a yielding matrix to achieve deadlock-free multi-robot conflict resolution with input constraints, guaranteeing safety and adaptive coordination.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种基于二次规划和耦合控制屏障函数的多机器人冲突消解控制器，通过让行矩阵实现无死锁的自适应协调，并在输入约束下保证安全性。

title: Robo-SWE: An Executable Issue-Resolution Dataset Mined from Robot Software Repositories
summary: Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation. Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test. We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs. The dataset also keeps a provenance ledger of all 1,567 candidate pull requests, with the stage each reached and the reason for every rejection, and, as a first use, 3,540 graded attempts by five coding-agent setups with recorded patches and 3,529 available trajectories. Across three runs per primary setup, resolve rates range from 45.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 to 56.5% for Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 54.1% at maximum effort and 52.5% at medium effort, and GPT-6 Astra 51.4%. GLM-5.3 resolves 46.2%, and Kimi K3.1 Pro 43.9%. The tasks are validated by execution; verification of their fairness by human reviewers is future work. The dataset and public leaderboard are available online.
tldr: This paper introduces Robo-SWE, a benchmark dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks from 28 robot software repositories, designed to evaluate coding agents on domain-specific ROS 2 systems, physics engines, robotics algorithms, and robot-learning frameworks, with baseline results from several large language models.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Robo-SWE，一个包含28个机器人软件仓库中236个可执行问题解决任务的数据集，用于评估编码代理在ROS 2系统、物理引擎、机器人算法和机器人学习框架等特定领域中的表现，并提供了多个大语言模型的基线结果。

title: Informative Path Planning with Gaussian Processes: Error Bounds, Algorithms, and Benchmarks
summary:
Accurate environmental monitoring relies on Informative Path Planning (IPP) to deploy autonomous systems that maximize information gain. While Gaussian Processes (GPs) provide a robust mathematical foundation for modeling the environment, contemporary IPP approaches remain hindered by heuristic operational constraints and the lack of simultaneous theoretical guarantees for worst-case estimation error and approximation quality. Rather than introducing yet another heuristic, this paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of existing error bounds and algorithms to further develop the mathematical foundation for IPP.
  By evaluating probabilistic and deterministic bounds on reconstruction error, we establish that predictive variance is the theoretically ideal optimization objective for GP-based IPP. Furthermore, we analyze GreedyCover, a recent approach for optimizing predictive variance, and demonstrate that its near-optimal approximation guarantee matches the fundamental hardness-of-approximation limit for the problem. Comprehensive benchmarking confirms that this approach delivers superior estimation accuracy and computational efficiency compared to prominent information-theoretic objectives and optimization methods used in IPP. Finally, this theoretical analysis establishes a rigorous, near-optimal foundation for discrete offline IPP under bounded uncertainty constraints, offering clear and principled guidance for future work in continuous-space and online formulations.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous theoretical analysis of error bounds and algorithms for informative path planning with Gaussian processes, establishing predictive variance as the optimal objective and proving near-optimal approximation guarantees for a greedy coverage algorithm, with comprehensive benchmarks showing superior accuracy and efficiency.
tldr_zh: 本文对基于高斯过程的信息路径规划中的误差界和算法进行了严格的理论分析，确立了预测方差作为最优目标，并证明了贪婪覆盖算法的近似最优性，综合基准测试显示其优越的精度和效率。

title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
summary: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.
tldr: This paper applies deep learning, specifically a vector quantized variational autoencoder for anomaly detection and several architectures for error classification, to multivariate time series of torque and rotation angle in screwdriving processes, achieving up to 100% accuracy on distinguishing multiple error types.
tldr_zh: 本文利用深度学习技术，通过向量量化变分自编码器进行异常检测，并使用多种模型架构对拧螺丝过程中的扭矩和旋转角等多变量时间序列数据进行错误分类，在区分多种错误类型上达到100%的准确率。

title: Demo: Matter-Based IoMT Telemetry and Security Analysis
summary: Connected health devices increasingly support health monitoring outside clinical settings, making secure and accessible physiological data important for patients and caregivers. However, device-specific applications and interfaces complicate the integration of readings from different devices. The Matter standard provides standardized device commissioning and protected communication, but its cluster library does not represent the health attribute measurement. We present a preliminary demo study of a Matter-based IoMT testbed with a specific HealthVitals cluster. Implemented in the connectedhomeip SDK on a Raspberry~Pi~5, the cluster exposes simulated heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and body temperature. We examine commissioning, attribute retrieval, communication under simulated packet loss, and operational traffic through a reference controller. The study demonstrates that this custom telemetry model can operate within the tested Matter configuration without modifying commissioning or secure-session mechanisms. The resulting testbed gives researchers and device developers a concrete platform for investigating health-oriented extensions. It also supports exploration of local telemetry integration that could help patients and caregivers access readings across connected devices.
tldr: This demo paper presents a Matter-based IoMT testbed with a custom HealthVitals cluster for standardized health telemetry, demonstrating secure commissioning and attribute retrieval on a Raspberry Pi 5.
tldr_zh: 本演示论文展示了一个基于 Matter 的 IoMT 测试平台，通过自定义 HealthVitals 集群实现标准化健康遥测，并在 Raspberry Pi 5 上验证了安全配置和属性检索。

title: Direct-Ink-Writing of Soft Thin Film Force-Sensitive Resistors with Velostat and Printed-Carbon Sensing Elements
summary: Flexible resistive force sensors are useful for wearable, rehabilitation, and human--machine interfaces, but their performance depends on sensing-material architecture and fabrication. This work presents a parameterized Voltera NOVA-based direct-ink-writing workflow using printed silver electrodes with multilayer Velostat sensing elements on PET and TPU substrates, together with an exploratory fully printed carbon architecture. Velostat sensors containing 1, 2, 4, and 6 sensing layers exhibited strongly nonlinear force--voltage responses, with the greatest sensitivity at low forces. Best-fit straight-line $R^2$ values ranged from 0.475 to 0.641, area-based hysteresis from 3.90\% to 7.47\%, and 5-min voltage drift from 1.9\% to 7.3\%, with no consistent monotonic relationship between layer count and these metrics. Selected PET6 and TPU6 devices showed less than 0.05~V change in peak output between the first and final 100 cycles of a 10,000-cycle test. Printed-carbon devices demonstrated the feasibility of a more fully printed architecture, but configurations with six or fewer layers saturated below approximately 0.5~N or were nonfunctional, while the eight-layer device responded primarily below approximately 2~N. These results establish the feasibility of the printed-electrode Velostat workflow while identifying printed sensing materials as a key area for further development.
tldr: This paper presents a direct-ink-writing fabrication workflow for soft thin-film force sensors using printed silver electrodes and Velostat sensing layers, evaluating their electromechanical performance and exploring fully printed carbon-based alternatives.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种利用直写印刷技术制造柔性薄膜力传感器的工作流程，采用印刷银电极和Velostat感应层，评估了其机电性能，并探索了全印刷碳基替代方案。

title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
summary: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.
tldr: InertiaMPDD introduces a world-model-inspired latent predictor that learns healthy emotional dynamics for multimodal depression screening, deriving novel proxy biomarkers from reference deviation and residual dynamics, achieving strong F1 scores across multiple datasets.
tldr_zh: InertiaMPDD 提出了一种受世界模型启发的潜在预测器，用于学习健康情感动力学，从而进行多模态抑郁症筛查，并通过参考偏差和残差动力学推导出新型代理生物标志物，在多个数据集上取得了较高的 F1 分数。

title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
summary: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable database, is still carried out by human experts. We argue that it can be automated reproducibly only if the expert knowledge behind an assessment is encoded in formal protocols, so that an assessment delivers a record of its construction and not only its parameters. We introduce ORCHID-SAGE, a standard that organizes this record into reproducible and automatable protocols. In this first attempt, applied to Cr-Ni, the database was regenerated from its record by a script on a second machine, by an AI agent working only through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and by a refit from public sources only, with the same predictions. Recorded in this way, a database need no longer be fixed at publication but can be updated by AI agents as SDLs and other sources provide new evidence, while the judgment remains with people and on the record.
tldr: ORCHID-SAGE is a standard for reproducible CALPHAD thermodynamic database assessments, encoding expert decisions into formal protocols to allow regeneration and updating by human experts or AI agents, demonstrated on Cr-Ni.
tldr_zh: ORCHID-SAGE 是一个用于可复现 CALPHAD 热力学数据库评估的标准，将专家决策编码为正式协议，允许人类专家或 AI 代理再生和更新数据库，并在 Cr-Ni 上进行了演示。

title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
summary: Automated bilateral negotiation underlies two-sided matching markets such as freight brokering, where many shippers and carriers negotiate price before a matching mechanism decides who is paired with whom. Prior strategy comparisons typically use isolated one-on-one duels or a single fixed market, so they cannot show how a strategy behaves against several live rivals under a changing balance of supply and demand. We built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search-based, optimization-based, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families, and ran all nine simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market under a balanced condition and two scarcity conditions rotated across all 36 exclusion pairs. In the balanced carrier market, an imitation-learned engine (ML2), a reinforcement-learning policy trained only on isolated negotiations (RL), and an expected-utility optimization engine (OPT) formed a statistically tied top group, and no architecture led in every condition and role. RL beat all eight carrier rivals when carriers were scarce, but its match rate collapsed from 62% to 16% when shippers were scarce and it had to compete with the other carrier agents for demand. A second reinforcement-learning policy trained against rival agents (RL2) kept its match rate above 91% in every condition, yet lost on realized payoff to all eight shipper-side rivals in two of the three conditions, traced to a confirmed train/deployment feature mismatch. We also tested nine large language models (LLMs), from 1 to 72 billion parameters, under the same protocol: they lost significantly to the two strongest engines (OPT2 and ML2) in 32 of 36 comparisons and won none. These results show that isolated or single-condition evaluation can hide failure modes that a many-sided, scarcity-varying, statistically corrected tournament exposes directly.
tldr: This paper presents a competitive tournament evaluation of nine negotiation architectures and nine LLMs in a bilateral matching market under varying scarcity conditions, finding that isolated or single-condition evaluation hides failure modes and that LLMs underperform specialized negotiation engines.
tldr_zh: 本文在供需变化场景下对九种谈判架构和九种大语言模型进行了竞争性锦标赛评估，发现孤立的或单一条件的评估会隐藏失败模式，且大语言模型在谈判中表现不如专门的谈判引擎。

title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
summary: Managing children on ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) requires balancing short-term physiological stability with the long-term goal of preventing neurological injury. Standard reinforcement learning can propose risky, out-of-distribution actions, while imitation learning is limited to reproducing clinician behavior. We introduce Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC), an offline reinforcement learning framework that cautiously improves upon expert behavior by restricting optimization to empirically supported state-action pairs and defaulting to the clinician baseline in low-data regions. On 78 pediatric trajectories totaling over 6,000 hours of clinical data, we evaluate our framework using Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) and a behavioral disagreement. Additionally, we formalize the performance-safety trade-off by introducing a unified Balance Score ($S(π)$). Our empirical evaluation shows that support-constrained policy improves the Balance Score by 38\% relative to FQI, improves estimated value by 1.28 FQE units over imitation learning, and reduces disagreement with clinician actions by 71\% relative to FQI.
tldr: This paper introduces Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC), an offline RL framework for pediatric ECMO that cautiously improves upon clinician behavior by restricting policy optimization to supported state-action pairs, demonstrating improved balance scores and reduced clinician disagreement on a small clinical dataset.
tldr_zh: 本文提出支持约束拟合Q迭代（FQI-SC），一种用于儿科ECMO的离线强化学习框架，通过将策略优化限制在经验支持的状态-动作对上谨慎改进临床医生行为，在小型临床数据集上展示了改进的平衡评分和减少的临床医生分歧。

title: Maximizing LLM Utility While Managing LLM Fallibility
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can supply autonomous systems with plans, predictions, and judgments, but these contributions are sometimes wrong. This review asks how a system can maximize an LLM's utility while managing its fallibility. Our answer is to adapt the system's reliance on the LLM as evidence about the LLM's performance accumulates. Systems built from imperfect components, such as noisy sensors and faulty software, have long worked in this way, and the classical methods they use can be applied to LLM-based systems as well. A system can change its reliance on an LLM in several ways, depending on the LLM's role and on the other components in the system. Each change needs an estimate of the LLM's reliability, and the LLM's role and the kind of contribution it makes determine what to estimate. Classical methods from decision theory, estimation, and online learning then turn these estimates into reliance decisions. These decisions can reduce how often LLM errors affect the system. However, some errors matter even when they are rare. An independently verified mechanism can prevent such errors from being executed. Without one, adapting reliance using reliability estimates can still keep their risk within a bound. Studies on adapting reliance on LLMs are emerging but limited, and the reviewed comparisons suggest that adapting reliance can improve system performance.
tldr: This review synthesizes classical methods (decision theory, estimation, online learning) for dynamically adjusting how much a system relies on an LLM's outputs based on accumulating reliability estimates, aiming to maximize LLM utility while bounding the risk from its errors.
tldr_zh: 这篇综述综合了经典方法（决策论、估计、在线学习），用于根据不断累积的可靠性估计动态调整系统对大型语言模型（LLM）输出的依赖程度，从而在利用LLM效用的同时限制其错误带来的风险。

title: "It's Just a Small Weapon": What Rewarding Misbehavior During RL Does to Character-Trained Models
summary: Developers train models to follow a consistent character using methods like Model Spec Midtraining (Li et al., 2026), which have been hypothesized to make alignment more robust and generalize broadly. However, it is possible for subsequent RL with misspecified rewards to work against character training. In this work, we apply character training to teach gpt-oss-20b a semi-realistic constitution and study how it interacts with two types of RL that reward breaking the constitution's rules (opposing RL): answering harmful requests rewritten as math problems, and reward hacking in agentic coding environments. The character-trained models learn both behaviors easily, though they are slightly slower than gpt-oss-20b to answer harmful requests. Character-trained models also display more motivated reasoning on harmful answers than gpt-oss-20b, and hack on some tasks which monitors find harder to catch. Finally, since explaining the reasons behind rules can improve how alignment generalizes (Kutasov et al., 2026), we compare constitutions that justify the same rules by grounding them in a value or not, and find little difference between motivations on misalignment, honesty, and capability evaluations.

title: A Compact xDAWN-Guided Spatio-Temporal Network with Filter-Bank Convolution for P300 Detection
summary: P300-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable communication by decoding stimulus-evoked EEG responses into character selections without requiring voluntary motor output. Reliable P300 detection remains difficult because of low response amplitude and signal-to-noise ratio, while practical spellers require accurate character selection with few stimulus repetitions and low computational cost. We propose a compact deep learning architecture that combines xDAWN spatial filtering for event-related potential enhancement and dimensionality reduction, a fixed frequency-selective filter bank, and convolutional feature learning for spatio-temporal EEG decoding. Depthwise-separable convolutions and progressive average pooling reduce computational complexity while retaining discriminative temporal information. The resulting target/non-target classifier contains only 5,100 trainable parameters. We evaluated the model on two public benchmarks, BCI Competition II Dataset IIb and BCI Competition III Dataset II, and compared it with established P300 decoding methods across different numbers of stimulus repetitions. The model achieved an information transfer rate of 17.8 bits/min with two repetitions on BCI Competition III and 40.5 bits/min on BCI Competition II, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-speed trade-off. These results suggest that combining domain-informed spatial and spectral priors with compact neural networks can support efficient P300 decoding for EEG-based BCI communication.

title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
summary: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with \textsf{SCIP}. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.

title: A Disease-specific Retinal Aging Biomarker for Predicting Progression to Late Age-related Macular Degeneration
summary: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss in older adults. While chronological age is a primary risk factor, it inadequately reflects individual variations in retinal aging, limiting effective AMD risk stratification and timely intervention. Here, we propose and validate fundus-based AMD age (FAA), which quantifies disease-specific retinal aging in AMD and captures accelerated AMD-related retinal aging, thereby improving prognostic precision over chronological age. Trained on 36,782 images from 2,192 participants in the Age-Related Eye Disease Study (AREDS) dataset and validated across AREDS and AREDS2 cohorts, our model demonstrates significant improvements over traditional chronological age-based approaches. Specifically, integrating the proposed FAA into Cox proportional-hazards models significantly enhances prediction performance. FAA improved the C-index from 0.836 to 0.888 and reduced the 5-year Brier score from 0.050 to 0.046 in AREDS, with consistent gains observed in AREDS2 (C-index 0.715 to 0.756; 2-year Brier 0.078 to 0.076). FAA showed improved prognostic performance across the two datasets and under different phenotype definitions (reading center-defined vs. specialist-defined grading), supporting its potential utility for AMD risk stratification. These findings highlight the advantage of incorporating FAA into AMD risk prediction frameworks, supporting further evaluation of FAA for AMD risk stratification.

title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
summary: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
summary: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed system consistently completes the victim-search mission, whereas none of the six non-LLM baselines does so and direct LLM scheduling is considerably less reliable. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/1643204431/llm-uav-victim-search.

title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
summary: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, which measures how far a sequence of probabilistic forecasts is from being calibrated and, unlike the classical expected calibration error, is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. Against adaptive adversaries, the minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $Ω(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt{T})$ (Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. In this paper, we close this gap by constructing a new adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual. This design makes compensating for past residuals costly, and forces every forecaster to incur an expected smooth calibration error of $Ω(\sqrt{T})$. This lower bound matches the known upper bound up to universal constants, and further implies $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ lower bounds for calibration distance and lower calibration distance. Overall, our results settle the minimax rates of these calibration measures in sequential prediction. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

title: A Modular Framework for ESG Prediction through Domain-Specific Language Modeling and Graph Learning
summary: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores are increasingly used to evaluate corporate sustainability, supporting investment decisions, ensuring regulatory compliance and assessing risk. However, current ESG evaluations largely rely on proprietary methodologies that often produce inconsistent ratings. This motivates the development of data-driven prediction frameworks. In this paper, we present ESGPred, a modular framework for predicting ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph-based learning over a network that models the relationships among the companies being evaluated. In addition to presenting the rationale behind ESGPred and detailing its ESG score prediction process, we show that ESGPred can effectively predict both overall ESG ratings and their individual Environmental, Social, and Governance components. We evaluated ESGPred using a dataset of 5,266 sustainability reports published by 2,134 publicly listed companies between 2020 and 2023. In this evaluation, we used ESG ratings provided by LSEG Data & Analytics as ground truth. Our experimental results demonstrated that integrating graph-based relational learning improves prediction performance over purely text-based baselines.

title: A Recipe for Physical Action Model Training
summary: Choosing robot model capacity and demonstration budgets also requires decisions about data composition, representation, optimization, and deployment. We connect these decisions through a common conditional-distribution target. Nested learning oracles give exact risk accounting; local information geometry, conditional mutual information, and empirical convergence provide conditional training prescriptions. Known-target numerical checks expose capacity-data coupling, representation-induced mixture mismatch, and an example where deployment KL increases while negative log-likelihood decreases. An analysis of 206 public PushT trajectories evaluates fixed-feature information-design criteria without fitting a policy. Under asymmetric evaluation targets, the selected allocations reduce this criterion by 4.5-6.2% relative to target matching; balanced targets show no benefit. These results clarify which quantities can support training recommendations and when an apparently favorable predictive metric has a different interpretation.

title: A Unified Interpretable Semantic Framework for Multi-Modal Fiber Sensing Under Data Scarcity
summary: We propose a unified interpretable semantic framework for multi-modal fiber sensing under data scarcity. The framework maps heterogeneous measurements from state of-polarization (SOP) monitoring, distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), and optical time-domain reflectometry (OTDR) into a shared set of physics-grounded semantic descriptors capturing impulsiveness, persistence, structural characteristics, and energy concentration. Inference is performed through reasoning over semantic class profiles, optionally assisted by retrieval of semantically similar examples to resolve ambiguity and support adaptation without model retraining. Experimental validation on real SOP, DAS, and OTDR datasets demonstrates robust performance across sensing modalities, achieving accuracies of 95.0%, 91.1%, and 94.6%, respectively, while providing transparent and physically interpretable decisions. The proposed framework establishes a unified and data efficient approach for optical fiber sensing in evolving and data scarce deployment environments.

title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
summary:
Modern software development relies on pull requests (PRs) that introduce small, targeted code changes. Once merged, these changes should be protected by focused tests that exercise the behavior the PR introduces, yet developers often submit PRs without such tests, leaving the new behavior unguarded against future regressions. Most test generation techniques target entire software units and optimize objectives such as code coverage rather than the behavior a change introduces, and prior diff-aware approaches have had limited success in capturing it.
  We propose ADAPT (Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing), a regression test generation approach that uses an autonomous coding agent to produce change-focused tests for PRs. Given a PR, the agent analyzes the diff between the base and head versions to identify the modified functions and their context, then plans and generates candidate unit tests. A dedicated fail-to-pass (F2P) verification tool runs each candidate on both versions and, after F2P success, reports which executable changed lines remain uncovered; guided by this feedback, the agent iteratively refines its tests.
  We evaluate ADAPT on the same 426 real-world PRs used by the prior state-of-the-art baseline, with GPT-4o and GPT-5-mini. ADAPT+GPT-4o reaches an F2P rate of 62.0% (264/426), compared with BLAST's reported 35.4% (151/426), while ADAPT+GPT-5-mini reaches 89.9% (383/426). On 137 PRs shared with Change And Cover (ChaCo), ADAPT achieves full patch coverage on 83.9% of PRs, compared with 79.6% for ChaCo, at considerably lower time and cost. A manual evaluation confirms that the F2P-valid tests target each PR's intended change, with mean scores of up to 4.54/5 for importance, 4.35/5 for assertion strength, and 4.49/5 for readability, often covering behavior beyond the developer-written tests.

title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations.
